subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.
reasoning:
I'm planning a static truck model built from simple geometric parts, roughly 7 meters long, 2.9 wide, and 3.2 tall, with wheels and a glow effect, keeping the structure simple since no skeleton or joints are needed.

I'm defining a palette of gunmetal, olive-dark armor, magenta accents, cyan glow, and hazard yellow, then laying out the chassis frame with side rails and cross members, four wheel axles with tires, hubs, and rims, plus the lower and upper cab hull boxes.

Working out the windshield and hood geometry, using tilted boxes rotated about the x-axis so the hood slopes down toward the front, calculating the sign convention needed to get the nose-down tilt right.

Now I'm planning the front details: a plow-style bumper with hazard stripes, glowing headlight bars, magenta grille slats, plus a roof light bar and antenna sensors on top.

I'm designing the side armor skirts with "2077" marking and magenta emblem stripes, then detailing the cargo bed as a ribbed armored container with a roof turret (ring, body, twin rotated-cylinder barrels), a side missile pod with glowing tube tips, and rear exhaust stacks, red taillights, and a hazard-marked rear door.

Adding fuel tanks, solar antenna array, rear ramp, and drone pad, then setting up helper functions for boxes, cylinders, and glow parts to keep the detailing loops clean. I'm working out ground clearance by setting wheel centers at the right height and orienting cylinders along X or Z axes with rotation values, planning to mirror components across the left/right side with a symmetry loop.

Now I'm detailing the cargo container with a patches-based camo paint using dark tones, keeping color count low, and designing the wheel assembly with tire, steel rim, glowing cyan hub, and bolt positions arranged radially around the wheel.

Checking wheel radius 0.7 keeps it just below the floor, close enough to work. Now I'm placing the turret on the cargo roof, aligning cab and cargo box heights so they overlap cleanly with the chassis rails, and figuring out skirt panel placement between the wheel axles to avoid collisions with the wheels themselves.

I'm adjusting wheel and hull widths so the fender arches sit properly over the wheels without clipping into the hull — settling on a hull width of 2.5 with wheels offset to 1.45 for a total vehicle width around 3.4, with the cargo bed a bit wider at 2.8. Now I'm ready to start writing the full model code at a moderate length.
